PHYS-AI-001.description: CNNs with hexagonal receptive fields vs square grids: hexagonal tiling has 13% fewer pixels for same coverage, isotropic neighborhoods, no axis-aligned bias. sqrt(3) geometry vs sqrt(2) geometry. Hexagonal CNNs outperform square CNNs on rotation-invariant tasks. Direct MDL argument: hexagonal is the minimum description of isotropic 2D structure.
PHYS-AI-001.name: Hexagonal CNN Architecture

PHYS-BS-001.description: Hypothetical bound state of pure gluons. Non-abelian self-interaction. Predicted by QCD lattice ~1.7 GeV. Connected to Yang-Mills mass gap (Millennium Prize).
PHYS-BS-001.name: Glueball

PHYS-C-001.description: First law of thermodynamics / Noether's theorem from time translation symmetry. Total energy of isolated system is constant. dE/dt = 0.
PHYS-C-001.name: Energy Conservation

PHYS-C-002.description: Noether's theorem from spatial translation symmetry. dp/dt = 0 for isolated systems.
PHYS-C-002.name: Momentum Conservation

PHYS-C-003.description: Noether's theorem from rotational symmetry. dL/dt = 0. Governs orbital mechanics, quantum spin.
PHYS-C-003.name: Angular Momentum Conservation

PHYS-CL-001.description: Two-body gravitational problem: elliptical orbits. T^2 proportional to a^3. Conserved Runge-Lenz vector gives closed orbits.
PHYS-CL-001.name: Kepler Orbits

PHYS-CL-002.description: Gravitational three-body dynamics. No general closed-form solution. Chaotic trajectories, sensitive dependence on initial conditions.
PHYS-CL-002.name: Three-Body Problem

PHYS-CL-003.description: Strange attractor, butterfly effect, positive Lyapunov exponent. Paradigm of deterministic chaos.
PHYS-CL-003.name: Chaos / Lorenz System

PHYS-CL-004.description: Differential gravitational force across extended body. F_tidal ~ (2GMr)/R^3. Causes ocean tides, Roche limit.
PHYS-CL-004.name: Tidal Forces

PHYS-CRYSTAL-001.description: Body-centered cubic (coord-8) to face-centered cubic (coord-12) transition under pressure/temperature. BCC sqrt(2)-neighbor geometry is brittle under shear; FCC/HCP hexagonal-close-packed geometry is robust. The sqrt(2)/sqrt(3) ratio distinguishes brittle from stable lattice geometry. Bain path is the minimal-energy transformation path.
PHYS-CRYSTAL-001.name: BCC-FCC Crystal Phase Transition

PHYS-F-001.description: Universal gravitational attraction F = GMm/r^2. Long-range 1/r^2 law.
PHYS-F-001.name: Gravity (Newtonian)

PHYS-F-002.description: Unified electric and magnetic force. U(1) gauge symmetry, photon-mediated. Maxwell equations.
PHYS-F-002.name: Electromagnetism

PHYS-F-003.description: SU(3) color force binding quarks. Asymptotic freedom, confinement, gluon-mediated.
PHYS-F-003.name: Strong Nuclear Force

PHYS-F-004.description: SU(2) force responsible for beta decay. W/Z boson mediated, parity-violating, short-range.
PHYS-F-004.name: Weak Nuclear Force

PHYS-GR-001.description: Belinsky-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz dynamics near a space-time singularity. Geometry undergoes chaotic oscillations (Mixmaster universe). In the billiard limit, dynamics maps to a particle bouncing in a hyperbolic triangle. Chaotic energy spectrum decomposes as product over primes in certain models, recovering primeon-gas-like partition function from pure geometry. Hossenfelder 2026 review.
PHYS-GR-001.name: BKL Singularity / Gravitational Billiards

PHYS-HP-001.description: Conjectured self-adjoint operator H whose eigenvalues are the nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) on the critical line. If such H exists and is a quantum Hamiltonian, then RH follows from self-adjointness (real eigenvalues). The central conjecture linking quantum mechanics to prime distribution since Hilbert-Pólya (1914/1930s).
PHYS-HP-001.name: Hilbert-Pólya Operator

PHYS-HP-002.description: Specific candidate for Hilbert-Pólya: H = xp (position × momentum). Classical trajectories are hyperbolic (unstable). Quantization requires boundary conditions that regularize; the resulting spectrum should approximate ζ-zeros. Berry-Keating (1999). Connects quantum chaos, semiclassical methods, and prime distribution.
PHYS-HP-002.name: Berry-Keating Hamiltonian

PHYS-KVN-001.description: Unitary lift of Hamiltonian flow to L^2(M, mu). Fills the central void of the physics ring in TF-IDF embedding.
PHYS-KVN-001.name: Koopman-von Neumann Operator

PHYS-N-001.description: Hexagonally arranged place-field firing in entorhinal cortex. sqrt(3)-spacing geometry is MDL-optimal for 2D coverage: achieves maximum coverage density with minimum cell count. Multiple spatial scales (modules) form Sidon-like non-repeating sum structure for path integration. Brittleness/robustness analogy: square grid would give ambiguous position readout.
PHYS-N-001.name: Grid Cell Navigation

PHYS-NT-001.description: Statistical mechanical system where each prime p contributes an independent oscillator with energy log p. Partition function Z(β) = Π_p (1 - p^{-β})^{-1} = ζ(β). Phase transition at β=1 (pole of zeta). Energy levels E = Σ a_p log p. Introduced by Spector (1990), Julia (1994). Bridge between multiplicative number theory and thermodynamics.
PHYS-NT-001.name: Primeon Gas

PHYS-PRIMON-001.description: Non-interacting Bose gas with one mode per prime p and single-primon energy E_p = log p. Z(beta) = zeta(beta). Hagedorn transition at beta=1. Ref: Julia, Les Houches 1990.
PHYS-PRIMON-001.name: Julia Primon Gas

PHYS-PT-001.description: Logarithmic capacity of a set E in the complex plane: cap(E) = exp(-V_E) where V_E is the Robin constant. Governs polynomial approximation, conformal mapping, equilibrium measures. Chebyshev constant = cap(E) for intervals. Direct connection to extremal polynomial problems (#1038, Chebyshev sublevel sets) and potential-theoretic Erdos problems (#671). The bridge between complex analysis and combinatorics via equilibrium measure.
PHYS-PT-001.name: Logarithmic Capacity

PHYS-Q-001.description: Core QM principle. System in linear combination of eigenstates until measured. Interference effects.
PHYS-Q-001.name: Quantum Superposition

PHYS-Q-002.description: Non-separable correlations. Bell inequality violation. Monogamy of entanglement. Resource for quantum computation.
PHYS-Q-002.name: Quantum Entanglement

PHYS-Q-003.description: Particle penetrates classically forbidden barrier. T ~ exp(-2*kappa*a). Alpha decay, STM, tunnel diodes.
PHYS-Q-003.name: Quantum Tunneling

PHYS-Q-004.description: QED radiative correction ~1058 MHz. Vacuum fluctuations plus self-energy. First precision test of QED.
PHYS-Q-004.name: Lamb Shift

PHYS-QC-001.description: Pisot substitution tilings with singular-continuous diffraction; deterministic aperiodic order, non-repeating but long-range correlated.
PHYS-QC-001.name: Quasicrystal Substitution Geometry

PHYS-R-001.description: Universal model F=-kx. Springs, pendulums, molecular vibrations, photon modes. Archetype of periodic motion.
PHYS-R-001.name: Harmonic Oscillator

PHYS-R-002.description: Pendulum demonstrating Earth rotation via precession. Period = 24h/sin(latitude). Slow modulation of fast oscillation.
PHYS-R-002.name: Foucault Pendulum

PHYS-R-003.description: Electrical resonance: omega=1/sqrt(LC). Energy oscillates between electric and magnetic fields. Foundation of radio.
PHYS-R-003.name: LC Circuit

PHYS-R-004.description: Acoustic resonance of air in cavity with neck. f=(c/2pi)*sqrt(A/(V*L)). Bottles, musical instruments.
PHYS-R-004.name: Helmholtz Resonator

PHYS-RADAR-001.description: Frequency-hopping patterns with bounded pulse-pair collisions. Side-lobe suppression from B_h[g] constraint. Ambiguity function framework.
PHYS-RADAR-001.name: Frequency-Hopping Radar Codes

PHYS-RMT-001.description: Spectral-radius envelope sigma_MP = epsilon*sqrt(W) of the noisy Ulam-Galerkin operator. Crossover matched to the gap 1 - tau*. Previously labeled GUE Random Matrix Ensemble; refined after EXP-DISS-KVN-001.
PHYS-RMT-001.name: Marchenko-Pastur Spectral Envelope

PHYS-RMT-GUE-001.description: N x N Hermitian random matrices with complex Gaussian entries. Wigner surmise spacing. Connected to Riemann zeros via Montgomery-Odlyzko. Ref: Dyson 1962, Mehta 3rd ed.
PHYS-RMT-GUE-001.name: Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE)

PHYS-S-001.description: Abelian gauge group of electromagnetism. Phase rotation of charged fields. Charge quantization.
PHYS-S-001.name: U(1) Gauge Symmetry

PHYS-S-002.description: Non-abelian gauge group of the weak force. Spontaneously broken by Higgs giving mass to W/Z bosons.
PHYS-S-002.name: SU(2) Symmetry

PHYS-S-003.description: Non-abelian gauge group of the strong force. Three color charges. Confinement: only color singlets observed.
PHYS-S-003.name: SU(3) Color Symmetry

PHYS-S-004.description: Symmetry group SO(3,1) of special relativity. Boosts plus rotations. Spacetime interval invariant.
PHYS-S-004.name: Lorentz Symmetry

PHYS-S-005.description: Charge-Parity-Time reversal. Exact symmetry in all QFTs. Connects particles to antiparticles.
PHYS-S-005.name: CPT Symmetry

PHYS-S-006.description: Local symmetry principle. Core principle of Standard Model requiring gauge fields.
PHYS-S-006.name: Gauge Invariance

PHYS-SIG-001.description: Pulse timing positions forming a Sidon set guarantee unambiguous radar: no two range-velocity pairs produce the same return. Uniquely decodable sum-channel code. Max density Sidon set = max radar pulses per bandwidth. Singer construction achieves channel capacity ~sqrt(N). Physics: information channel capacity. Math: Sidon set density conjecture h(N)~sqrt(N).
PHYS-SIG-001.name: Radar Ambiguity / Sidon Codes

PHYS-SP-001.description: Gap between smallest eigenvalue (0) and second-smallest (lambda_2) of graph Laplacian. Governs mixing time of random walks, connectivity, expanders. Fiedler value. Cheeger inequality: h^2/2 <= lambda_2 <= 2h. Direct math-physics bridge: same spectral gap appears in quantum Hamiltonians (ground state vs first excited), random matrix theory, and Erdos spectral graph problems (#89 cluster).
PHYS-SP-001.name: Spectral Gap (Laplacian)

PHYS-SPIN-002.description: 1D frustrated Ising-like chain with 3-body interaction J(s_a + s_b - s_{a+b}). Ground-state degeneracy 2^{N/2} matches sum-free count.
PHYS-SPIN-002.name: Frustrated Ising Chain (3-body)

PHYS-T-001.description: Ideal heat engine. Maximum efficiency eta=1-T_cold/T_hot. Reversible limit of thermodynamics.
PHYS-T-001.name: Carnot Cycle

PHYS-T-002.description: Abrupt change in matter state. First-order: latent heat. Second-order: critical exponents, universality.
PHYS-T-002.name: Phase Transitions

PHYS-T-003.description: Universal behavior near second-order transitions. Power-law scaling, critical exponents. RG theory, universality classes.
PHYS-T-003.name: Critical Phenomena

PHYS-T-004.description: Second law: dS/dt >= 0. Irreversibility, arrow of time. Near equilibrium: sigma = sum J_k * X_k.
PHYS-T-004.name: Entropy Production

PHYS-T-005.description: Diffusionless solid-state phase transition: BCC->FCC/BCT via Bain correspondence. sqrt(2) contraction along one axis, sqrt(2) expansion transversely. Square geometry is metastable (zero off-axis slack); hexagonal geometry stable. Mechanism: coord-4 lattice has no slack under shear. Same geometric mechanism as square-packing brittleness in math.
PHYS-T-005.name: Martensitic Transformation
